title: Systemic failure-mode matrix and chaos runbook for multi-region inference
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Objective: Produce a canonical failure-mode matrix + executable chaos runbook for Redwood Inference that covers region loss, selective GPU pool exhaustion, dependency blackholes (KMS, internal config service, control-plane DB), and circuit-breaker hysteresis. Deliverables:

1) Failure-mode matrix: catalog of failure classes, expected observable symptoms (latency, token-per-second drops, queue depth, error rates), likely root causes, and recommended mitigations and playbook steps.

2) Chaos runbook: concrete experiments (commands/playbooks) that ops/eng can run in staging and pre-prod, with safe blast-radius controls, guardrails, and automated rollback. Each experiment must map to one or more SLOs and have explicit success/failure criteria.

3) Telemetry & assertions: list of Prometheus/Telemetry checks, SLO guardrail thresholds, and dashboard links used to validate behavior. Include synthetic load harness snippets for ramp and soak testing.

4) Postmortem checklist & automated evidence collection: a small set of scripts that capture traces, logs, KV cache snapshots, and routing decisions relevant to each scenario.

Scope notes: Focus on cross-region request routing, model fallback behavior when a variant is unavailable, continuous batching under pressure, KV/prefix cache correctness when connections are flaky, and interactions between circuit breakers and autoscaling. This ticket is specifically about documenting and implementing the experiments and runbook (not the runtime fixes themselves).

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical failure-mode matrix published to Confluence (link included in comments).
- At least 6 executable chaos scenarios merged into the chaos repo (PR link in comments).
- Metrics-based assertions (PromQL) for each scenario that can be run in CI to validate SLO degradation or graceful degradation behavior.
- A 1-hour tabletop drill plan that uses the runbook and lists roles, escalation paths, and key post-drill actions.

Risks & constraints: Avoid running destructive experiments against production control plane or customer-dedicated pools. Some dependency blackhole experiments require mock proxies or stubbed services to avoid customer impact. All experiments must have an opt-out circuit and explicit approval from SRE lead before running against any environment other than staging.
